title: Energy-Efficient Drone Design with Solar-Powered Hybrid Propulsion System for Extended Flight Duration
content: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), commonly known as drones, face fundamental limitations in flight duration due to battery constraints, typically restricting operations to 20-60 minutes. This paper proposes an energy-efficient drone design leveraging a solar-powered hybrid propulsion system to achieve extended endurance, targeting 24 hours continuous flight and beyond under realistic conditions. Drawing inspiration from adaptive edge intelligence frameworks, the design integrates high-efficiency photovoltaic (PV) cells, lithium-based batteries, reinforcement learning (RL) for power management, and swarm coordination for fleet optimization. Key innovations include wing-integrated solar harvesting, RL-driven mode switching between solar-direct cruise and battery-boost climb, and bio-inspired energy sharing among drone swarms. Simulations and extrapolated prototypes demonstrate 4-5x endurance gains, with applications in persistent surveillance, environmental monitoring, and disaster response. Evaluations confirm 30-40% energy savings versus conventional designs, while maintaining payload capacity >2 kg.
